subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus
subsystems.role: carries the main spacecraft and two probes to the waiting point and supports them during the flyby.

subsystems.name: Science payload
subsystems.role: characterises the comet nucleus, coma and dust environment during a brief high-speed encounter.

subsystems.name: Deployable probes
subsystems.role: two small spacecraft released before flyby to sample different regions of the coma at the same time.

subsystems.name: Communications
subsystems.role: sends science data back across deep space and receives commands.

subsystems.name: Guidance, navigation and control
subsystems.role: points instruments at a target that may not be known until shortly before encounter.

subsystems.name: Thermal and power management
subsystems.role: keeps electronics operating from loiter at Sun-Earth L2 through a close solar approach.

buildSteps.title: Design for an unknown target
buildSteps.detail: Engineers size the trajectory, encounter speed and instrument suite for a comet that may not be discovered until after launch.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the spacecraft bus and probes
buildSteps.detail: Lightweight structures, propellant tanks, solar arrays and release mechanisms are built and assembled.

buildSteps.title: Build and test instruments
buildSteps.detail: Cameras, spectrometers and dust detectors are calibrated to work in the cold, high-speed flyby environment.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and qualify
buildSteps.detail: The main craft and probes undergo vibration, thermal-vacuum and electromagnetic testing together.

buildSteps.title: Launch and cruise to Sun-Earth L2
buildSteps.detail: The spacecraft is launched into deep space, travels to the Sun-Earth L2 point and commissions its systems.

buildSteps.title: Loiter and watch the sky
buildSteps.detail: It waits for up to three years while ground-based surveys search for a dynamically new comet entering the inner solar system.

buildSteps.title: Retarget and approach
buildSteps.detail: Once a target is chosen, controllers compute an intercept trajectory and release the two probes on slightly different paths.

buildSteps.title: High-speed flyby
buildSteps.detail: The main craft and probes fly through the coma at up to 70 km per second, sampling different regions simultaneously.

buildSteps.title: Transmit and analyse data
buildSteps.detail: Recorded images and spectra are sent to Earth and compared with remote observations of the comet.

prerequisites.why: missions already orbit Sun-Earth L2 and can serve as a staging point for an intercept.
flybys have been achieved, but targeting a newly discovered comet on short notice is harder.
small probes need low-mass, low-power cameras and dust sensors.
the main craft must relay data from two probes released just before a fast flyby.
a suitable dynamically new comet must be found in time to plan the encounter.
dust impacts at tens of kilometres per second can damage or destabilise the spacecraft.

pathway.milestone: mission design and construction of the main craft and two probes
pathway.unlocks: a launch-ready interceptor that can wait for an unknown comet.

pathway.milestone: launch and cruise to Sun-Earth L2
pathway.unlocks: a parking orbit from which the spacecraft can be retargeted.

pathway.milestone: loiter for up to three years and select a dynamically new comet
pathway.unlocks: a flyby of material that has never been heated by the Sun.

pathway.milestone: high-speed flyby with simultaneous probe sampling
pathway.unlocks: direct comparison of the nucleus, coma and dust environment.

pathway.milestone: follow-up comet interceptors or sample-return concepts
pathway.unlocks: deeper insight into the primordial chemistry of the early solar system.
